segments: 508 Book of the Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
for she mounted the throne beside the King of Kings, and he took her by her hands and placed in her ear a ring with costly pearls.
And at this time when Baghdad was captured,
the lord of Mayperqat,
who was al-Ashraf, son of Malik Ghazi, son of al-Adil the Great,
meditated rebellion.
And he impaled a Syrian priest from the region of Bidlis,
who had come to him from the Great Khan with a yarligh,
and he drove away the Mongol governors from his presence.
And he arose and went to Damascus to Malik al-Nasir,
and he sought help from him to attack the Tatars,
and to restrain them from descending upon Syria,
and, if possible, to drive them away also from Baghdad.
Malik al-Nasir, however, dismissed him with empty promises,
and he returned and came to Mayperqat, his city.
And as soon as he arrived,
the armies of the Tatars surrounded him,
and the Georgians {Arwāne} of Baishan,
standing at their head being
Ashmut, son of the King of Kings.
And they built a wall against it,
and set up mangonels,
and began to wage war from outside vigorously,
and those on the inside [fought] against them even more vigorously.
And thus it remained uncaptured for a period of two years.
Now after Baghdad was taken,
and the armies had shut up Mayperqat,
envoys began to follow continuously from the King of Kings to Malik al-Nasir,
demanding of him that he go to serve him.
And because his grandees were not pleased with his going,
he made an arrangement and sent his son Malik al-Aziz with treasures, offerings, and great gifts in the autumn of the year one thousand five hundred and seventy of the Greeks [1258 AD];
and he stayed there all winter.
And in the spring he returned and came to Aleppo after the Feast of the Resurrection and said to his father:
"The King of Kings commanded me and said:
'It was not you we sought, but your father;
now, therefore, if he is peaceful, let him come,
otherwise we are coming to him.'"
And that Malik al-Nasir remained halting between two opinions {cages}:
it was not possible for him to stay, out of fear of the Tatars,
nor could he go, lest his grandees and servants rise up against him and kill him;
and he was bewildered and terrified.
1 meditated {variant reading}.
2 a precious pearl.
